description: Understand core database concepts and database management system software, including the evolution of database systems, the role and overview of DBMS software, and the major areas studied in database systems.

Understand the relational model of data, including general data model concepts and the basic structure of relations. Explain the purpose of algebraic query language in expressing relational operations and reasoning about queries at a conceptual level.

Understand data normalization and apply normalization techniques in relational database design using functional dependencies, rules about functional dependencies, and relational schema design principles, including normal forms 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, and BCNF as mechanisms for improving database schema structure.

Model an application's data requirements using high-level database modeling techniques, especially the Entity-Relationship model, design principles, ER constraints, and weak entity sets. Translate conceptual models into relational schemas, including conversion from ER diagrams and subclass structures to relations.

Be proficient in SQL, including Data Definition Language (DDL) for defining database structures and implementing constraints such as primary and foreign keys, UNIQUE, and CHECK constraints using Microsoft SQL Server. Use Data Manipulation Language (DML) to perform basic queries, multi-relation queries, nested queries, aggregation queries, and database modifications using INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements.

Understand T-SQL database programming concepts in Microsoft SQL Server and work with database views, cursors, stored procedures, functions, and triggers, including the use of triggers to enforce database constraints. Understand transaction concepts in database applications.
Apply database indexes in relational database design to support query optimization and improve query performance in practical database applications.
